articles.title: Three killed in Russia as Ukraine claims US floated NATO membership option
articles.summary: Zelenskyy says the US asked for the first time whether Kyiv would cede land to Moscow in exchange for the NATO bid.
articles.body: A Ukrainian drone attack has killed a mother, father and their 24-month-old daughter at their home in Belgorod, a Russian region bordering Ukraine, according to Russian authorities. The deadly attack came on Saturday in Proletarsky, about 20km (12 miles) from Ukraine’s border as Russia’s Ministry of Defence claimed the army intercepted 29 Ukrainian drones overnight, including several over the Moscow region. In turn, Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 96 drones from Friday evening, of which 81 were shot down or electronically suppressed as of early Saturday. It reported hits at eight locations and falling debris at two others, while a local power supplier reported outages in parts of northeastern Sumy. Meanwhile, in Friday’s comments to reporters that were under embargo until Saturday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said United States negotiators had asked during this week’s Abu Dhabi talks whether Ukraine would withdraw its troops from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, the transatlantic military alliance. Zelenskyy said the question had been raised for the first time but that no concrete offer existed. Zelenskyy maintained that Ukraine would not withdraw its troops but could put the issue to a referendum if Kyiv received firm security guarantees, funding for its armed forces and money for reconstruction. Donbas comprises Donetsk and Luhansk, two eastern Ukrainian regions partly occupied by Russia. Moscow demands a Ukrainian withdrawal from areas Kyiv still controls, while also opposing Ukraine joining NATO, whose members pledge to defend one another. Zelenskyy said on Friday that he would not amend Ukraine’s constitution to make it neutral, arguing the move would not guarantee lasting security. Ukraine has been defending itself, with Western assistance, against a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022. This past week brought a resumption of US-mediated direct talks between the Russians and Ukrainians, which raised hopes of an early end to the war. However, apart from renewed prisoner exchanges, there appears to have been little progress. European representatives are set to take part in the next round of talks. Zelenskyy said the European Union and NATO are Europe’s “only real security” and that Moscow’s bid to review the continent’s security was “dangerous because … it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations”.

Russia sends major business delegation to Kabul for business talks with the Taliban
articles.summary: A Russian deputy prime minister led a 70-strong Russian delegation to Afghanistan, pursuing deals on transport, logistics, agriculture, and health products with the Taliban.
articles.body: Russian deputy prime minister Alexei Overchuk was welcomed by a guard of honour when he arrived in Kabul on Thursday with a delegation of 70 Russian business people to conduct business talks with the Taliban government, Afghan officials said.Overchuk met Taliban prime minister Mohammad Hassan Akhund, the deputy prime minister for economic affairs Abdul Ghani Baradar as well as foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.According to a statement by the Afghan government published on X, Abdul Ghani Baradar described to the Russians Afghanistan's potential for economic development and investment, pointing to "strategic location, abundant resources and a workforce of 24 million people".Abdul Ghani Baradar invited Russian companies to invest in agriculture, mining, constructions of roads, railways and factories, and to create a special economic zone in Afghanistan, while expressing his wish to expand exports of Afghan agricultural products to Russia.The deputy prime minister also asked Russia to "provide the necessary facilities for Afghan products to be supplied to Russian markets and to cooperate in reducing transport and transit costs".A Russian news agency quoted Alexei Overchuk as saying that the Russian delegation represent companies that are already operating in Afghanistan and that "many others want to start operating in this country."Overchuk said that the companies represented in the delegation work in the fields of transport, logistics, agriculture and pharmaceuticals and that the Afghan government is interested in Russian chemical fertilisers, as well as in "building fertiliser production plants on Afghan soil".Overchuk estimated that trade between Russia and Afghanistan in the first eight months of 2026 had more than doubled, reaching over 349 million dollars.Russia officially recognised the Taliban government in July 2025, being the only state to have taken such a step since the Taliban seized power in August 2021, after the withdrawal of the United States.Although no country other than Russia has formally recognised the new Afghan regime, the Taliban authorities have so far held high-level talks with many states and have established specific diplomatic and economic relations with some governments.

OSCE may fail to agree on 2027 chairmanship — Russian envoy
articles.summary: Some countries are engaged in nonstop shuttle diplomacy in search of a solution, Dmitry Polyansky said
articles.body: VIENNA, November 14. /TASS/. Member states of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) are actively holding diplomatic consultations on which country will chair the organization in 2027, but they may fail to reach consensus, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE Dmitry Polyansky told TASS. "I expect we’ll find some way forward. But we can’t rule out that possibility entirely," he said when asked whether the talks could end without an agreement. In that event, OSCE Secretary General Feridun Sinirlioglu would most likely oversee the organization’s work for a time, though that would require further decisions. "The OSCE is a fairly resilient organization, so I think it will find a way forward even in that scenario," the diplomat noted. "Some countries are engaged in nonstop shuttle diplomacy in search of a solution. The Americans are particularly active," Polyansky added. The envoy doubted that the issue would be fully resolved before the OSCE Ministerial Council meeting in Lugano in early December. He suggested that participants could reach some understandings at the meeting and formalize them later. Polyansky previously said Cyprus and Georgia are seeking the 2027 OSCE chairmanship. According to him, Turkey is blocking Cyprus’s bid while Georgia’s prospects are highly uncertain.

articles.title: Nikoloski: respect for the Constitutional Court shows institutional maturity
articles.summary: As a Government, we are making every effort to establish a functional system of the rule of law as the foundation of a democratic state, and here, of course, one of the key actors is the Constitutional Court, which has a special and irreplaceable role in preserving the constitutional order and protecting fundamental rights and freedoms, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport Aleksandar Nikoloski…
articles.body: As a Government, we are making every effort to establish a functional system of the rule of law as the foundation of a democratic state, and here, of course, one of the key actors is the Constitutional Court, which has a special and irreplaceable role in preserving the constitutional order and protecting fundamental rights and freedoms, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport Aleksandar Nikoloski said in his address at the fourth annual conference of the Forum of Balkan Constitutional Courts, held in Ohrid on the topic “Contemporary Challenges to the Rule of Law: The Role of Constitutional Courts.” Nikoloski stressed that the role of the Constitutional Court is particularly important in this time of rapid social, technological, and political changes. As he put it, “that is why institutions must be stable, institutions must be resilient, and institutions must survive political changes.” The independence, professionalism, and integrity of constitutional judges and of the Constitutional Court are key to fulfilling this function. The rule of law implies not only the adoption of high-quality decisions, but also their respect and implementation. The executive and legislative branches have the responsibility to create the conditions for the full implementation of the decisions of the Constitutional Court, which very often also mean a correction of certain decisions that may have been taken without sufficient analysis and without sufficiently taking all the facts into account, and sometimes even with some other intention. That is why the foundation of the Constitutional Court is precisely this — to help make corrections where corrections need to be made, Nikoloski pointed out. He noted that respect for constitutional justice is an indicator of a state’s institutional maturity and democratic responsibility. That is why we strive to respect the Constitutional Court and to give it the place it deserves in the state-legal order. The independence of the judiciary should, of course, not be understood in isolation from the other institutions, but rather as a guarantee of impartial and objective decision-making, and also as a way of improving society. Mutual control and balance among the three branches of power — and here, of course, the Constitutional Court as a separate body — play a significant role in maintaining a functional state, Nikoloski emphasized in his address before constitutional judges from the country and abroad. The Deputy Prime Minister also referred to the new challenges, such as digitalization and artificial intelligence, which on the one hand can be an advantage, but on the other hand also a threat. Of course, knowledge, experience, and the human factor remain irreplaceable, and I cannot agree with certain debates that are being conducted, that even in this area — in the area of respecting the Constitution, in the area of implementing the Constitution, and in the area of implementing and respecting the laws — we should rely on artificial intelligence. I think that is wrong, and I think it is something that we need to think about very seriously as a state and as states, because this is a broader debate, not only in our country, but I repeat, I believe that is not the path we should follow, because knowledge and personal experience are something that is irreplaceable and that no machine can do, Nikoloski said. At the closing of the Forum of Balkan Constitutional Courts, Deputy Prime Minister Nikoloski stressed that a strong state does not mean only a strong executive power, but a limited executive power, a state with strong and independent institutions, institutions that complement each other and control one another. Therefore, as a representative of the executive branch, as Deputy Prime Minister, I can say that as a Government we will do everything and we are doing everything for this system to continue to function and to be further developed, Nikoloski said.

3 killed, 11 rescued as perimeter wall collapses in Kenya
articles.summary: Three people were killed after a perimeter wall collapsed at an active construction site in the Riverside area of Nairobi, Kenya's capital, on Saturday, Xinhua reports. Bramwell Simiyu, chief officer for disaster management and coordination at the Nairobi County Government, said 11 construction workers were rescued alive from the rubble and rushed to nearby medical facilities with severe injuries.
articles.body: Three people were killed after a perimeter wall collapsed at an active construction site in the Riverside area of Nairobi, Kenya's capital, on Saturday, Xinhua reports. Bramwell Simiyu, chief officer for disaster management and coordination at the Nairobi County Government, said 11 construction workers were rescued alive from the rubble and rushed to nearby medical facilities with severe injuries. Simiyu said 39 workers were on-site when the collapse occurred at around 11:30 a.m. (0830 GMT), noting that multi-agency emergency response, search, and rescue teams were actively operating at the construction site. "Preliminary site assessments confirm that the main building on the property was still at the excavation and foundation stage, with no upper floors erected at the time of the incident," he said at the site. The county government said 14 workers had been accounted for and confirmed safe at the scene, while search-and-rescue teams were still working to establish the whereabouts of the others. The county government said hospital admission checks and on-site accountability exercises were ongoing to establish the status of all workers listed in the site's records. Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud said a team was on the ground to coordinate the rescue operations and conduct investigations. "We have three fatalities and others are injured. We want to know what happened and how," he said. This came a day after a building under construction collapsed and killed six workers in the Syokimau area of Nairobi. Several buildings have collapsed in Kenya in recent years, with experts pointing to poor regulatory enforcement and a lack of routine safety inspections by government officials.

ALDE resolution calls on "Georgian Dream" to "end the ban on opposition parties, immediately release political prisoners, repeal the foreign agents law, and hold new elections"
articles.summary: The ALDE Party has adopted a resolution titled "Protecting Political Pluralism and Ending Political Repression in Georgia." Through this document, ALDE calls on the Georgian authorities to "end the ban on opposition parties, release political prisoners, and call new elections."
articles.body: The ALDE Party has adopted a resolution titled "Protecting Political Pluralism and Ending Political Repression in Georgia." Through this document, ALDE calls on the Georgian authorities to "end the ban on opposition parties, release political prisoners, and call new elections." "We condemn: 'Georgian Dream's' authoritarian repressions, including court proceedings aimed at banning parties, politically motivated persecution, penalties for online criticism, restrictions on civic space, and impunity for the abuse of force, all of which violate international standards. An end to the banning of opposition parties, including circumvention through successor parties, and political exclusion based on party affiliation or employment by foreign-funded organizations; political participation must be guaranteed. The immediate and unconditional release of political prisoners and those detained for exercising their fundamental rights. The dropping of politically motivated sabotage charges against opposition leaders, the protection of peaceful demonstrators, journalists, human rights defenders, and international organizations, and ensuring the monitoring of fair, independent court proceedings. An end to detentions and disproportionate fines for peaceful protests and expression, including online criticism; punitive provisions must be repealed. The repeal of repressive foreign agents and funding restrictions; the restoration of the ability for independent media, civil society, and human rights defenders to operate freely; the implementation of Venice Commission and OSCE recommendations; and independent investigations into torture, ill-treatment, and attacks. The holding of new, free, and fair parliamentary elections with impartial administration, international observation, unrestricted opposition participation, and protection against intimidation," the document states. The text of the resolution was distributed by the press service of the "Droa" party.

articles.title: Prosecutor's Office requests bail as a preventive measure for Giorgi Pataridze and Ramaz Pirtskhalava, charged in the attack case against Davit Peikrishvili
articles.summary: The Prosecutor's Office is requesting the application of bail as a preventive measure against Giorgi Pataridze, the former Director General of the Penitentiary Service, and Ramaz Pirtskhalava, the former Director of Penitentiary Establishment No. 8, who are charged in the case concerning the attack on Davit Peikrishvili.
articles.body: The Prosecutor's Office is requesting the application of bail as a preventive measure against Giorgi Pataridze, the former Director General of the Penitentiary Service, and Ramaz Pirtskhalava, the former Director of Penitentiary Establishment No. 8, who are charged in the case concerning the attack on Davit Peikrishvili. The time of the court hearing, where the imposition of the preventive measure is to be deliberated, remains unknown. In the same case, pre-trial detention has already been imposed as a preventive measure on so-called criminal authorities Vato Kipiani, Avtandil Bilanishvili, Shota Kipiani, Pavle Gotsiridze, and Davit Kacharava. For reference, the Prosecutor's Office filed charges against the former Director General of the Special Penitentiary Service Giorgi Pataridze, the former Director of Penitentiary Establishment No. 8 Ramaz Pirtskhalava, and the so-called criminal authorities Vato Kipiani, Shota Kipiani, Avtandil Bilanishvili, Pavle Gotsiridze, and Davit Kacharava over the beating of inmate Davit Peikrishvili—who is linked to criminal circles—inside his cell. The investigation charges Giorgi Pataridze with exceeding official powers, and Ramaz Pirtskhalava with abuse of official authority. As for the so-called criminal authorities, they have been charged under the article covering intentional less grave bodily harm committed by a group against Davit Peikrishvili.

Dodik Goes to the US Once Again: Following a Meeting with Trump’s Supporters, He Now Seeks Contacts with Democrats
articles.summary: The SNSD Leader, Milorad Dodik, has once again traveled to the United States, just days after attending a meeting of MAGA movement supporters in Florida linked to US President Donald Trump.
articles.body: The SNSD Leader, Milorad Dodik, has once again traveled to the United States, just days after attending a meeting of MAGA movement supporters in Florida linked to US President Donald Trump. His next stop is Chicago, where, in addition to meeting with the members of the Serb community, he intends to make contact with the representatives of the Democratic Party. Ahead of his trip, appearing on the podcast “Provjereno,” Dodik announced that he would attend the consecration of a church in Chicago, at the invitation of the local Serb community. But he emphasized that the visit will not be limited to religious and social activities. According to him, he plans to have talks with influential political actors who achieved significant results in the recently held elections for the US Congress. He described Chicago as the “epicenter of Democrats,” hinting that he intends to expand his circle of political interlocutors in the United States. After Years of Harsh Criticism, Dodik Changes Approach Toward Democrats. The announcement that he will get close to the US Democrats represents a significant shift in Dodik’s public appearance toward that political party so far. Over the past years, he has often harshly criticized democratic administrations in Washington, especially the administration of former President Joe Biden, which he once termed a “mortal enemy of the Republika Srpska.” He had a similar stance towards the Student List in Serbia, which he criticized before its victory at the parliamentary elections. After the election success of this political movement, Dodik began making significantly more positive assessments about its representatives. He now announces attempts to establish closer relationships with the US Democrats, although he emphasized that cooperation with the Republicans and Donald Trump’s administration remains his top priority. Dodik believes that there is an understanding within the current US administration of his political views and goals in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Lobbying in the US and Dodik’s Political Goals in BiH Dodik’s questions and unannounced political contacts come at a time when authorities of Republika Srpska are continuing with lobbying activities in the United States of America. For years, Dodik has been advocating for the possibility of Republika Srpska seceding from Bosnia and Herzegovina while contesting individual state institutions and competencies. The question regarding the status of Republika Srpska appears in a contract that the Government of Republika Srpska concluded with the lobbying company Dickens & Madson. According to the statements from that contact, they planned to allocate at least four million dollars. Speaking about the policy of the US President, Dodik expressed his support for the approach that implies the United States abandoning the building of foreign states and nations. “We support the policy of stopping the building of other people’s states and nations. This means that BiH will not be built and that there will be no insistence on ‘Bosnians’ who do not exist and who never existed,” Dodik stated. His statements reflect his long-standing opposition to the concept of strengthening a shared Bosnian-Herzegovinian identity and state institutions. Igor Dodik Among Possible Candidates for Republika Srpska Prime Minister In addition to international political relations, Dodik also spoke about the upcoming formation of the new government of Republika Srpska, which is expected to happen in the next few days. He confirmed that Željko Budimir, the current Minister of Interior of Republika Srpska, is expected to retain his position in the new composition of the entity’s government. His statement that he does not rule out the possibility of his son, Igor Dodik, being proposed as the Prime Minister of the Republic of Srpska drew particular attention. Igor currently serves as the organizational secretary of the SNSD , and his father considers him one of the party’s most promising personnel. Nevertheless, Dodik emphasized that he does not want to rush his appointment to one of the most responsible political functions in the entity. As a reason, he cited the complexity of the political issues awaiting the future government, including those relating to the status of Bosnia and Herzegovina. “He is undoubtedly a good solution for the future,” Dodik said, adding that he does not want to prematurely expose his son to the political challenges that lie ahead. According to Dodik, the choice of the future Prime Minister of the Republic of Srpska will ultimately come down to two candidates. Although he confirmed that Igor Dodik is one of the names under consideration, he did not reveal the identity of the second potential candidate. The final decision on who will lead the new entity government has yet to be made. In the meantime, Dodik continues his international activities, striving to establish contacts with representatives of both leading US political parties while simultaneously participating in decisions regarding the future composition of power in the Republika Srpska, BHRT writes.

articles.title: HDZ BiH President Announces Intense Negotiations on Government Formation
articles.summary: President of HDZ BiH Dragan Čović announced that new intense negotiations on government formation at the federal and state level will begin on November 23rd, emphasizing that his party’s goal is to form the new convocation of the Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina […] The post HDZ BiH President Announces Intense Negotiations on…
articles.body: President of HDZ BiH Dragan Čović announced that new intense negotiations on government formation at the federal and state level will begin on November 23rd, emphasizing that his party’s goal is to form the new convocation of the Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina as soon as possible. Following today’s session of the Presidency of HDZ BiH, Čović spoke about the upcoming political negotiations, possibilities of establishing the parliamentary majority, and obligations that Bosnia and Herzegovina must meet to accelerate the European integration process. According to him, HDZ BiH is trying to create political prerequisites for forming the executive branch, while expecting that the indirect election of delegates to the houses of peoples will be completed. Čović stated that representatives of his party have already held talks with political representatives of all three constituent peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as with international partners, aiming to find solutions that would enable the establishment of new government institutions. The FBiH Government and the Council of Ministers of BiH should be formed in the Same period. Speaking about deadlines, the president of HZD BiH announced that the new federal government should be accompanied by the Council of Ministers of BiH. We want the FBiH budget in December, as well as the BiH budget. The wish would be, as is the legal deadline for the FBiH Government, for the BiH Council of Ministers to be in the package,” Čović stated. He announced that talks on government formation will be intensified as of November 23, when more concrete alignment of political stances and possible partnership is expected. But he emphasized that HDZ BiH has yet to start the negotiations on distribution of ministerial positions. As he explained, on behalf of HDZ BiH, there has been no discussion so far regarding specific portfolios in either the future Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the Council of Ministers of BiH. A significant part of his address was dedicated to European integration, assessing that Bosnia and Herzegovina must show greater political determination and accelerate the fulfillment of obligations expected of it. He expressed the expectation that cooperation with political partners from Croatia could contribute to a new momentum in the process of bringing Bosnia and Herzegovina closer to the European Union. He specifically referred to Montenegro’s progress, stating that its European path should serve as an additional incentive to domestic political actors. “I am sure that by the end of the year Montenegro will fulfill all conditions for the EU; everyone says that by the end of the sixth month it will have full membership, so the question arises: where are we,” Čović said. According to his assessment, Bosnia and Herzegovina possesses the political and institutional capacities to independently initiate necessary reforms. He believes there is a possibility of adopting two important laws from the European agenda in the House of Representatives of the Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which would make an additional step forward toward the European Union. “We do not expect someone else to do that for us. I think there are enough of us that we can lead that process,” said the president of HDZ BiH. Čović also touched upon political changes in Serbia and their potential impact on relations in Bosnia and Herzegovina. He assessed that the change of government in the neighboring country should not have a particularly pronounced impact on internal political processes in BiH, stating that he does not expect significant external interference in that regard. In continuation, he reiterated that HDZ BiH will strive to contribute to the fastest possible establishment of government, expecting that upcoming negotiations will enable reaching an agreement on new executive structures. As key priorities, he singled out the formation of the Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Council of Ministers of BiH, the adoption of budgets by the end of the year, and the acceleration of legislative activities necessary for the continuation of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s European path.

Uzbekistan Sets Winter Gas Supply Priorities for 2026–27
articles.summary: Uzbekistan will prioritise households, schools and hospitals in natural gas distribution during the 2026–2027 heating season under a government resolution.
articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — Uzbekistan will prioritise households and social facilities in natural gas distribution during the 2026–2027 autumn-winter season, the Ministry of Energy said. The measures are set out in a Cabinet of Ministers resolution that will remain in force from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. Residential buildings, schools, kindergartens, hospitals and other social institutions will receive priority access to available gas resources. The resolution also provides for measures to ensure supplies to strategically important consumers. The Ministry of Energy, together with Uztransgaz, Khududgazta’minot and other responsible organisations, will prepare gas supply forecasts covering both ten-day periods and individual days. The schedules will take into account available natural gas volumes and weather conditions. They must be submitted monthly to the Republican Commission for Preparation for the Autumn-Winter Season for approval no later than the 25th of each month. If pressure in main gas pipelines falls or available gas volumes change unexpectedly, the distribution schedules will be revised promptly. Priority supplies to households and social facilities must be maintained. The Republican Commission will approve supply schedules for the following month, covering regions and major wholesale consumers, by the last day of each month. The Council of Ministers of Karakalpakstan and the regional and Tashkent city administrations, together with regional branches of Khududgazta’minot, will organise gas distribution among districts and cities based on the approved schedules. They will also give priority to residential buildings and social institutions. During periods of severe cold, temporary restrictions may be imposed on consumers in other categories to ensure stable gas supplies to households and social facilities.

articles.title: Two Men Jailed for Three Days Over Insults in Tashkent
articles.summary: A Tashkent court sentenced two men to three days of administrative arrest for insulting a young man after a dispute on the metro.
articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — A court in Tashkent sentenced two men to three days of administrative arrest each for insulting a young man following a dispute on the metro, the capital’s police department said. According to law enforcement authorities, a man identified as A. became involved in a verbal altercation with the young man after he refused to give up his seat in a metro carriage. The dispute continued after they left the metro. A. followed the young man to a food service establishment in Chilanzar district. The police department said A. continued to insult the victim in a public place, violating accepted standards of behaviour. He recorded the incident using a camera built into his glasses. The victim said he did not understand why the strangers had behaved that way. He also said a video featuring him had been posted on social media that day without his consent. One of the offenders said he had published the footage to gain content and likes. He apologised for what had happened. The Chilanzar District Criminal Court found both men guilty of petty hooliganism under Article 183 of Uzbekistan’s Code of Administrative Responsibility. Each was sentenced to three days of administrative arrest.

articles.title: Europeans mum on Abu Dhabi talks at latest OSCE meeting — Russian mission
articles.summary: Russia’s permanent representative to the organization Dmitry Polyansky stressed that the Europeans came with old talking points
articles.body: VIENNA, November 14. /TASS/. At the latest meeting of the OSCE Permanent Council, European delegations reiterated their previous positions on the Ukrainian conflict and did not mention the Abu Dhabi talks even once in their statements, Russia’s permanent representative to the organization Dmitry Polyansky told TASS. "The Europeans seemed completely out of touch. They came with their old talking points. They didn’t even mention the word 'Abu Dhabi' once, as if it were happening on another planet," the diplomat emphasized. According to him, only the Ukrainian and US delegations mentioned the talks in Abu Dhabi. At the same time, the Ukrainian representatives spoke in their usual Russophobic tone, while the US representative emphasized the importance of the efforts all sides are making in connection with the negotiation process.

articles.title: Tajikistan’s per capita gas consumption falls to 19 cubic metres in 2025 - Eni
articles.summary: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Tajikistan’s per capita natural gas consumption amounted to 19 cubic metres in 2025, down from 25 cubic metres in 2024, according to Italian energy company Eni’s World Energy Review 2026.
articles.body: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 14. Tajikistan’s per capita natural gas consumption amounted to 19 cubic metres in 2025, down from 25 cubic metres in 2024, according to Italian energy company Eni’s World Energy Review 2026. Eni’s figures show that per capita natural gas consumption in Tajikistan stood at 24 cubic metres in 2019, before declining to 23 cubic metres in 2020 and recovering to 24 cubic metres in 2021. The indicator then fell to 19 cubic metres in 2022, rose to 21 cubic metres in 2023 and reached 25 cubic metres in 2024, before falling back to 19 cubic metres in 2025. Eni did not provide a figure for 2015. For comparison, the regional indicator for Russia and Central Asia stood at 2,615 cubic metres in 2025, down from 2,658 cubic metres in 2024. It amounted to 2,199 cubic metres in 2015 and 2,310 cubic metres in 2019, dipped slightly to 2,308 cubic metres in 2020 and peaked at 2,677 cubic metres in 2021. It then declined to 2,550 cubic metres in 2022 and 2,535 cubic metres in 2023. Meanwhile, Tajikistan’s population reached 10.8 million in 2025, compared with 10.6 million in 2024, according to Eni. The company reported year-on-year growth of 1.8% and a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 2.2% over 2015–2025. The country’s population increased from 8.6 million in 2015 to 9.5 million in 2019, then to 9.7 million in 2020 and 10 million in 2021. It rose further to 10.2 million in 2022, 10.4 million in 2023 and 10.6 million in 2024, before reaching 10.8 million in 2025.

articles.summary: The delegation will include representatives of the European Commission, the EU Council, Germany, France, Italy, and Poland, as well as the UK
articles.body: LONDON, November 13. /TASS/. EU leaders at Friday's summit in Dublin agreed on a delegation for expert-level talks with Russia that will include representatives of the European Commission, the EU Council, Germany, France, Italy, and Poland, as well as non-EU member United Kingdom, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported, citing a European source. The negotiating team will be the same one that flew to Abu Dhabi this week. Russia, the United States and Ukraine held talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky led the Russian delegation, while Foreign Intelligence Service chief Rustem Umerov headed the Ukrainian delegation. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich and UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan were also present at the negotiating table when the talks began. Despite statements from French officials, no Europeans attended the meeting. Kremlin Aide Yury Ushakov said European representatives consulted with the Ukrainian and US sides on the sidelines of the talks. He noted that discussions on whether Russia might meet with the Europeans and what form such a meeting might take would be based on the outcome of the Abu Dhabi talks. Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova pointed out that the Europeans had exposed themselves by holding Coalition of the Willing exercises to rehearse the deployment of foreign military contingents to Ukraine just before the Abu Dhabi talks. She stressed that while the Europeans talk about peace, negotiations and their place at the negotiating table, they are doing exactly the opposite by sustaining, funding and arming the terrorist Kiev regime.
